_note: Actuators are nearly all cylinders from the outside, so almost every prompt asks for a cutaway or an exploded view and names the one internal feature that identifies the mechanism. Where a motor and its transmission look alike, the differentiator is stated explicitly (brushes on a commutator ring, an elliptical wave generator, cycloidal discs on ring pins). Anchor is 2, the BLDC, because it sets the cutaway convention the rest inherit. Do not name copper anywhere: the house palette is steel-blue accents only, and naming the material makes the model add a warm accent that breaks the set.
_partNote: Class images for the explorer tiles, written after the per-entry attempt above was abandoned. These are exterior views of whole objects and never cutaways. The failure last time was that classes I, II, III and V are all a cylinder with a shaft, so the prompts reached inside for the identifying mechanism and the internal geometry came back wrong. Here the classes are kept apart by outside proportion and mounting instead: a slim upright motor can, a toothed belt looped over two very different pulleys, a squat wide joint puck with a bore through it, a heavy hydraulic barrel with a rod and eye mounts, a long flat magnet track with a carriage riding on it, a small rigid layered column, and a soft braided muscle hanging free. Each renders at about 74px, so every prompt asks for one centered object with a bold silhouette and no fine detail.
style: Minimalist technical illustration, the style of a precise patent drawing crossed with an isometric product sketch. Uniform-weight dark slate-gray ink linework with sparse, muted steel-blue accent shading (hex 4E7AA8) on a plain very light warm-gray background (hex F2F3F1). Three-quarter isometric view, single centered subject, generous margins. No text, no labels, no callouts, no logos, no humans, no background scenery, no drop shadows. Clean, engineered, calm. Strictly two colors plus the background: dark slate-gray line and muted steel-blue fill. Every material, including wire, windings, coils, magnets and terminals, is drawn in that same palette. Absolutely no copper, brass, bronze, gold, orange, red, yellow or green anywhere, even where the real object would be that color. Favor open, airy linework with large unfilled light areas over heavy solid gray shading; the drawing should read as line art, not as a rendered solid model.

prompts.1: Cutaway of a brushed DC motor, with the rear half of the housing removed so the commutator and brushes dominate the foreground and are the largest features in the drawing: a commutator built as a drum of many separate narrow metal bars divided by thin insulating gaps, and two rectangular carbon brush blocks sitting in brush holders, each pushed radially inward by a small coil spring so its flat face presses on the bars at opposite sides. Behind them a wound rotor on a laminated core and curved magnets on the housing wall. Two wire leads. The sliding brush-on-bar contact must be unmistakable and must not be hidden inside the body.
prompts.2: Cutaway of a brushless DC motor: a cylindrical housing whose inner wall carries a stator of many wound teeth pointing inward, and a central rotor with rectangular permanent magnets arranged around its circumference. Output shaft on a front bearing, three thick phase wires leaving the rear, no brushes anywhere.
prompts.3: Cutaway of a NEMA-flange stepper motor: a square mounting flange at the front, a rotor built from two toothed iron cups with fine axial teeth around a central disc magnet, and stator poles carrying coils whose pole faces have matching fine teeth. Emphasize the fine tooth pitch on both rotor and stator. Four wire leads.
prompts.4: An integrated servo motor as one finished unit: a cylindrical motor body with a small gearbox at the output end, a thin encoder disc visible through a cutaway at the rear, and a compact drive circuit board stacked behind it carrying a single connector. One cable leaves the assembly.
prompts.5: A frameless torque motor shown exploded into two coaxial rings, separated along the axis: a large-diameter thin rotor ring with many magnets tiled around its outer face, and a matching stator ring with many wound teeth on its inner face. Both rings have a very large hollow center bore. No housing, no shaft, no bearings.
prompts.6: Cutaway of a planetary gearbox: a central sun gear meshing with three planet gears mounted on a carrier plate, all running inside an internally toothed ring gear. Gear teeth clearly drawn at every mesh. Output shaft from the carrier, input shaft to the sun.
prompts.7: A harmonic strain-wave drive exploded into three coaxial parts along the axis: an elliptical wave generator plug fitted with a thin flexible ball bearing, a thin-walled flexible cup with external teeth around its open rim, and a rigid internally toothed circular spline ring. Show the flexspline visibly deformed into an ellipse, meeting the ring gear teeth at the two ends of the major axis and clear of them elsewhere.
prompts.8: Cutaway of a cycloidal drive, deliberately not a gear train: there are no involute gear teeth anywhere in the drawing. A thick disc with a smooth scalloped wavy lobed outer edge sits off-center on an eccentric input shaft, and its lobes press outward against a ring of separate straight cylindrical pins standing upright around the inside of the housing like a circle of posts. A second identical lobed disc sits behind the first, rotated half a lobe. Round output pins pass through oversized circular holes bored through both discs. Emphasize the eccentric offset and the many lobes contacting pins at once.
prompts.9: A ball screw: a long shaft with a helical groove machined along it, and a nut cut away to reveal a train of small steel balls riding in the groove and a return tube looping over the outside of the nut to recirculate them. The nut carries a bolted mounting flange.
prompts.10: A belt transmission spanning a distance: a small motor with a toothed pulley at one end, a long synchronous belt with clearly drawn teeth running to a much larger toothed pulley at a robot joint at the other end, and a small idler pulley tensioning the span. The two pulleys are far apart.
prompts.11: A quasi-direct-drive actuator: a wide, flat, large-diameter pancake brushless motor with a high pole count, and a single compact planetary stage shown in cutaway at its output face. Squat proportions, wide relative to its length. Thick phase wires and a rear encoder disc.
prompts.12: A series-elastic actuator laid out in line: a motor, then a gearbox, then a visibly separate coil spring pack coupling the gearbox output to the output link, with a small encoder reading angle on each side of the spring. The spring in the load path is the focus.
prompts.13: A variable-stiffness joint driven by two motors: one motor drives the output link directly, while a second smaller motor turns a cam that tightens a pair of curved leaf springs pulling against each other on opposite sides of the joint. The antagonistic spring pair is the focus.
prompts.14: A servo-hydraulic actuator: a heavy hydraulic cylinder with its piston rod extended and clevis mounts at both ends, carrying a servo valve block bolted to its midsection, with two stiff high-pressure hoses entering the valve block through fittings.
prompts.15: An electro-hydrostatic actuator as one sealed self-contained unit: a cylinder with a compact electric motor and a small gear pump integrated into a manifold at one end, plus a small fluid reservoir on the manifold. No external hoses at all, only a single electrical cable.
prompts.16: A pneumatic setup in two parts: a cylinder with four tie rods running the length of its barrel, end caps, an extended rod, and two push-to-connect air fittings; beside it a manifold rail carrying a row of three small solenoid valves with their coils on top.
prompts.17: A linear motor: a flat straight track plate tiled with alternating rectangular magnets, and a coil forcer block riding just above the track, guided by a linear rail alongside. A flat cable leaves the forcer. Show the air gap between forcer and magnet track.
prompts.18: Cutaway of a cylindrical voice coil actuator: a permanent magnet assembly with an annular air gap, a coil wound on a light bobbin riding inside that gap, a central output shaft, and a flat spider flexure suspending the bobbin. No bearings, no gears.
prompts.19: Cutaway of a tubular solenoid, which is not a motor: there is no rotor, no output shaft, no bearings and nothing that rotates. A single coil is wound around a straight bobbin inside a rectangular iron frame that closes the magnetic path, and a plain cylindrical iron plunger slides straight along the bore, protruding from one end of the body with a return spring behind it. Two wire leads. The motion is purely straight-line push along the axis.
prompts.20: A piezoelectric stack actuator: a square column built from many very thin ceramic layers with interleaved metal electrodes visible along the two side faces, held in a preload housing with a domed contact tip at the top. Two fine wires. Emphasize the layer count.
prompts.21: A silicon MEMS comb drive at extreme magnification, viewed at a three-quarter angle: two interdigitated arrays of fine comb fingers, one array anchored to the substrate and the other carried on folded serpentine suspension springs, all etched in silicon with visible sidewalls and anchor pads.
prompts.22: A shape-memory alloy actuator: a thin straight nitinol wire held between two crimped terminal lugs, contracting to pull a small pivoting lever arm against a bias coil spring. Fine electrical leads at each crimp. The wire is thin, straight and taut.
prompts.23: A McKibben pneumatic artificial muscle shown contracted: a cylindrical rubber bladder inside a braided sleeve whose diamond mesh pattern is clearly drawn, crimped metal end fittings at both ends, one air hose entering the top. The muscle bulges at its middle and is visibly shortened, lifting a small weight below.
prompts.24: A HASEL electrohydraulic actuator stack: several flat flexible pouches stacked vertically, each partly filled with liquid dielectric and carrying a flat electrode patch over its outer end. The electrode regions have zipped closed, pushing fluid into the free end and contracting the stack. Two very thin high-voltage leads.
prompts.25: Two string actuators side by side: on the left a small high-speed motor twisting a pair of parallel cords into a tight shortened helix that pulls a lever; on the right a coiled-polymer fiber that looks like a tight helical spring wound from twisted polymer line, hanging with a small weight on it.

partPrompts.1: A single electric motor can standing upright on its rear end cap, seen three-quarter: a slim cylinder about two and a half times as tall as it is wide, with a rolled seam around the barrel, a flat front end cap on top, and one short plain round output shaft standing straight up from its center. A small round connector and two fine leads at the base. Exterior view only, not a cutaway: nothing inside is visible. No gearbox, no mounting flange, no piston rod, no hoses.
partPrompts.2: A toothed belt drive lying alone on a flat surface, seen three-quarter: one small pulley at one end and a pulley about three times its diameter at the other, with a single endless toothed belt wrapped around both and running taut along the two straight spans between them. The size difference between the two pulleys is the point of the picture. No motor, no housing, no frame, and no shafts beyond a short stub through the center of each pulley.
partPrompts.3: A single integrated robot joint module standing on a flat surface, seen three-quarter: a wide flat drum roughly three times as wide as it is thick, like a thick puck, with a large hollow bore straight through the middle, a ring of evenly spaced bolt holes around its output face, and one thick cable leaving the side of the rim. Exterior view only, not a cutaway. Squat and disc-shaped, clearly not a tall motor can, and nothing sticks out along the axis.
partPrompts.4: A hydraulic cylinder lying at an angle on a flat surface, seen three-quarter: a heavy round barrel with a smooth rod extended from one end, a ring-shaped clevis eye mount at each end of the assembly, and two short port fittings standing up from the side of the barrel with no hoses attached. One object, exterior only, no pump, no valve stack, no robot.
partPrompts.5: A linear motor axis lying flat and straight, seen three-quarter: a long low flat track plate tiled along its length with a row of plain rectangular magnet tiles, and one compact rectangular carriage block riding above the track with a clear air gap underneath it, a flat cable trailing from its rear. Long, flat and low to the surface. Not a cylinder: no barrel, no piston rod, no round housing anywhere.
partPrompts.6: A piezoelectric stack actuator standing upright by itself on a flat surface: a small rigid square-section column, hard-edged and straight-sided, built from a stack of layers drawn as maybe a dozen bold horizontal lines across its side faces rather than a fine texture, with a small domed contact tip on top and a flat base below. Two fine wire leads at the base. Rigid and geometric, not soft and not braided; no shaft, no housing, no cylinder.
partPrompts.7: A pneumatic artificial muscle hanging free by itself, seen three-quarter: a soft round tube covered by a braided sleeve with a bold coarse diamond mesh pattern, crimped metal end fittings at the top and bottom, and one short air stub at the top. The tube bulges visibly at its middle so it reads as fat and shortened rather than as a straight hose. One object hanging in the air, no robot, no frame, nothing rigid.
